blocks.html:
Tucked into the top two floors of a 120-year-old Chinatown shophouse that genuinely used to be an opium den, Opium is the bar that debuted on Asia's 50 Best Bars 2025 at No. 43, and also landed on the World's 50 Best Bars extended list at No. 92. Downstairs in the same building sits Potong, one of Asia's 50 Best Restaurants, so climbing the stairs here feels like discovering a side of Yaowarat most people walk straight past without ever looking up.

The menu is called liquid surreality, and it earns the name: modern cocktail technique meets Thai ingredients you rarely see in a glass, from oyster salt to banana liqueur. There are close to 50 cocktails and mocktails, plus four house-made gins, each drawing its character from a different region of Thailand. The drink everyone talks about is the Opium Oath, inspired by old Chinese blood oaths and finished with a splash of fake blood made from Por Kun Ear Boh, a traditional remedy that was actually sold in this building back when it was a medicine shop. Behind the bar is Matteo Cadeddu, an Italian bartender whose career runs through Australia, Singapore and Mumbai; the bar itself is the creation of Arnon 'KK' Hoontrakul.

The room trades the gritty nostalgia you might expect from the name for something sleek and low-lit, the kind of place built for a slow night and a real conversation. Getting here is easiest via the MRT Blue Line to Wat Mangkon station, then a short walk into Yaowarat toward Vanich 1 Road. Seating is limited and this is a reservation-first speakeasy, so message ahead on Instagram at @opm.bkk before you go.

faq.q: How do I get to Opium? Which BTS or MRT is closest?
faq.a: Take the MRT Blue Line to Wat Mangkon station, then walk into Yaowarat toward Vanich 1 Road. The bar is on the upper floors of the same building as Potong.
Yes, booking is recommended. Seating is limited and it runs as a reservation-first speakeasy, so message ahead on Instagram at @opm.bkk before you visit.
Prices sit in the premium range, roughly 400 to 550 THB per cocktail, with cocktails, mocktails and gin tasting flights on offer.
The talked-about pour is the Opium Oath, finished with fake blood made from a traditional remedy, alongside the liquid surreality menu built on Thai ingredients like oyster salt and banana liqueur.
